## What makes a hospital network “advantaged” under TEAM?

CMS TEAM pays — and claws back — on the **full 30-day episode**, not the index admission alone. Systems that already control (or tightly contract) post-acute care, employ the surgeons who generate episodes, and share a single EHR for discharge visibility start with structural advantages documented in earlier bundled-payment literature (Dummit et al., 2016; Finkelstein et al., 2018).

Brand reputation and academic status help quality scores; they do **not** automatically lower SNF length of stay. The networks below appear frequently on the March 2026 TEAM roster by hospital-name matching in Rainfall’s directory. Counts are **approximate** (naming is inconsistent across CCNs) and meant for strategic prioritization, not securities disclosure.

<BlogFastFacts label={"Fast Facts — Network footprints (name-match)"} items={["HCA family (incl. ## Which national and multi-state systems show up most?

Deep dives: **HCA** and **AdventHealth** network guides. Region context: Territory 4 (South & Midwest) for HCA/AdventHealth; Territory 1 for Kaiser/Providence; Territory 2 for Gulf Ascension/Ochsner dynamics.

<div class="blog-table-scroll not-prose">

| System (name-pattern) | Approx. TEAM sites | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HCA (TriStar / HealthONE / etc.) | ~29 | Largest for-profit multi-territory cluster; PAC playbooks scale |
| Kaiser Permanente | ~19 | Prepaid integration; employed physicians; owned pathways |
| AdventHealth | ~16 | Florida/Sun Belt density; ambulatory + PAC adjacency |
| Ascension | ~12 | Regional clusters sharing faith-based PAC relationships |
| Providence | ~9 | PNW / West integration across T1 markets |

</div>

## Which regional systems punch above their weight?

**New Jersey:** Hackensack Meridian and RWJBarnabas together organize much of the state’s 44-hospital TEAM market — dual-system density that independent NJ hospitals must underwrite with explicit SNF contracts.

**New York:** Northwell and peer multi-hospital systems can standardize orthopedic pathways across many CCNs inside the 109-hospital NY–NJ metro Core-Based Statistical Area (CBSA).

**Minnesota:** Fairview, Allina, and HealthPartners show the Twin Cities integrated-nonprofit pattern inside Territory 1’s 30 Minnesota hospitals.

**Colorado / Denver:** UCHealth, Intermountain (former SCL), and HCA HealthONE compete inside a 21-hospital Denver CBSA — integration is the battleground, not whether TEAM applies.

## What should independent and single-hospital boards do?

You cannot fake a 20-hospital EHR overnight. You **can** (1) join or build a preferred SNF panel with readmission SLAs, (2) put episode analytics in front of the orthopedic and spine chiefs weekly, (3) align gainsharing compliantly with employed and affiliated surgeons, and (4) stop planning against a 741 roster. See *How to prepare for CMS TEAM* and the hospital-count explainer.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which hospital network has the most CMS TEAM hospitals?

By Rainfall’s name-pattern matching on the March 2026 roster, the HCA family is the largest cluster (~29 sites), followed by Kaiser (~19) and AdventHealth (~16).

### Does being an academic medical center guarantee TEAM success?

No. Academic quality helps clinically, but episode profitability hinges on post-discharge spend. Several high-prestige Northeast AMCs face elevated readmission and PAC cost pressure.

### How were network counts estimated?

Case-insensitive name matching against the 721-hospital territoryHospitals.json directory. Counts are approximate because CMS rows do not include a standardized system ID.
